disclaimer: Reminder reference only - NOT legal authority. Season dates and limits are set by regulation and can change. Always verify current regulations with the Prince Edward Island Department of Environment, Energy and Climate Action (Forests, Fish and Wildlife Division) before hunting or trapping. Trapping in Prince Edward Island is governed by the Wildlife Conservation Act, R.S.P.E.I. 1988, c. W-4.1, the Fur Harvesting Regulations (EC663/04) and the Hunting and Trapping Seasons Regulations (EC592/16). This dataset is for the separate Canada clone of the app and is provisional research data, not yet final.

license_summary.certified_traps: Body-gripping traps for beaver, raccoon, muskrat and weasel (on land) and beaver/muskrat (underwater) must be approved traps listed in Schedule C of the Fur Harvesting Regulations - PEI's adoption of the Canadian Trap Certification Program (FIC) list. See the 'aihts' section of this dataset.
license_summary.course: Trapper Education Course (approved trapper education program) required for a first trapping licence: Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 2(1)(a)(ii) (age 16+) and s. 2(2) (junior). Courses are held twice a year, usually April and October; free for ages 12-15, $20 for ages 16+ (Trapping Information Centre). Since September 2025, certified trappers must also complete continuing education to maintain eligibility, fully phased in by 2029 (Government of PEI news release, September 16, 2025).
license_summary.fees: Trapping licence $10.00 (18+) and junior trapping licence $5.00 (Schedule B, Fur Harvesting Regulations, as amended by EC305/13; HST not included) - no newer official fee source was found in this pass, so treat as to-confirm. Wildlife Conservation Fund (WCF) licence: $20/year, $13/year for ages 65+, no fee under 16 (Trapping Information Centre; WCF page). Fur-bearer hunting licence $5 (resident, all age classes; no fee for Canadian Armed Forces members/veterans); non-resident hunting licence $75 seasonal / $60 three-day (Buy a Hunting Licence Online service page). Snowshoe hare snaring licence $5. Trapper Education Course $20 (16+), free 12-15.
license_summary.harvest_report: Fur dealers must keep records and report monthly during open season and within 30 days of a season close (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 13). A trapper must, on request by a conservation officer, provide information on the trapping of any fur-bearing animal whose green hide or carcass they possess (s. 10(2)). The annual summaries include a Trapper Harvest Log; whether returning a trapper harvest report is mandatory was NOT verified in this pass - see verification.known_gaps. There is no pelt tagging or sealing requirement in the Fur Harvesting Regulations.
license_summary.hunting_furbearers: Raccoon, red fox, coyote and red squirrel may be hunted under a fur-bearer hunting licence ($5 resident). Beaver, mink, muskrat, skunk and weasel may be taken ONLY by trapping (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 9(1)(f)). A fur-bearer hunting licence holder may sell the pelts of raccoon, coyote, red fox or red squirrel to a licensed fur dealer (s. 12(3)). Snowshoe hare hunting (Oct 1 - Mar 31, daily limit 5) is under the general hunting licence; hare snaring (Nov 1 - Feb 28) needs its own $5 Snowshoe Hare Snaring Licence.
license_summary.licence_types: Trapping licence; junior trapping licence; fur-bearer hunting licence; general hunting licence; snowshoe hare snaring licence; fur dealer's licence; fur export permit. A trapping licence expires on March 31 following the date of issue (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 2(8)). Trapping licences are sold in person at Access PEI offices and the Forests, Fish and Wildlife office, 183 Upton Road, Charlottetown (Trapping Information Centre); hunting licences are also sold online.
license_summary.permission: Landowner permission is required before setting traps (Trapping Information Centre; Fur Harvesting Regulations framework). September 2025 changes added permission requirements for traps on private land, a higher permission standard for snares, and a landowner right to remove traps set without permission (news release). Snares have been prohibited on public land since the September 2025 changes, and trapping is restricted/closed on about 3,525 hectares of listed public land.
license_summary.quotas: PEI has NO licence quotas and NO bag limits for trapping: Schedule II of the Hunting and Trapping Seasons Regulations sets open seasons with no daily, season, or possession limits for any trapped species. The only bag limit in this dataset is snowshoe hare hunting (5/day).
license_summary.report_violation: Report a violation to a Conservation Officer: leave a detailed message anytime at 902-368-4884 (Government of PEI, 'Report a Violation to a Conservation Officer', updated February 2, 2026). Forests, Fish and Wildlife Division: 902-368-4683 / 1-866-368-4683.
license_summary.trap_check: Every trapping device must be examined at least once every 72 hours; traps designed to hold an animal alive at least once a day; snares designed to kill red fox or coyote at least once every 48 hours (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 9(1)(h)-(i), 2015 consolidation - confirm against the current consolidation, see verification.known_gaps).
license_summary.trapping_licence: A trapping licence is required to trap fur-bearing animals (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 2). Eligibility: held a valid trapping licence within the previous 5 years, OR age 16+ and successful completion of an approved trapper education program; junior licence for under-16s who have completed the program. Each licensed trapper is assigned a permanent trapper registration number, and every trap or snare set must be clearly identified with it (s. 2(4)-(5)). A current Wildlife Conservation Fund licence is also required.

verification.confirmation_notes: Seasons were verified against the Hunting and Trapping Seasons Regulations (EC592/16), Schedules I and II (office consolidation current to September 15, 2018, read in full), cross-checked against the Fur Harvesting Regulations (EC663/04, office consolidation current to September 12, 2015, read in full), the official 2020/2021 summaries (which document the coyote October 15 foothold amendment), and two independent extractions of the official 2026 Hunting Summary quoting its page numbers. Licensing, fees, trap rules, check intervals and Schedule C were verified against the Fur Harvesting Regulations text and official princeedwardisland.ca pages (Trapping Information Centre, Buy a Hunting Licence Online, Wildlife Conservation Fund, Report a Violation). PEI furbearer seasons use fixed calendar dates only - there are no relative dates ('second Saturday of...') to compute for the species in this dataset, so no calendar computation was required; February 28, 2027 is confirmed as the last day of February 2027 (2027 is not a leap year) for the coyote close. regulation_year_confirmed is FALSE because the two 2026-27-specific items in known_gaps (the current consolidated regulations as amended in 2025, and the official 2026 Trapping Summary) could not be read directly in this session.
known_gaps: The official 2026 Trapping Summary PDF was not read directly: PDF links on princeedwardisland.ca could not be extracted with this session's tools and the site rate-limited page fetches. Trapping dates rest on the Seasons Regulations as amended by changes documented in official summaries through 2021, corroborated by 2026-dated extractions of the current summaries. Resolve by reading the official 2026 Trapping Summary PDF (linked from the Trapping Information Centre) and diffing every date.

The 2026 Hunting Summary was read via two independent secondary extractions quoting its page numbers (truenorthhunter.ca, huntscout.app), not the official PDF itself. The extractions agree with each other; re-verify against the official PDF before launch (same class of blocker as Ontario's mirror-copy Hunting Summary).

Hunting close dates: the 2018 consolidation of Schedule I reads March 30 for raccoon, coyote and snowshoe hare hunting; the 2026 Hunting Summary reads March 31. This dataset follows the 2026 summary (March 31). The amending instrument was not read; confirm against the current consolidation of the Seasons Regulations.

Coyote foothold opener: the 2018 consolidation of the Seasons Regulations (s. 2(4)) reads November 1; the official 2020 summary documents the opener moving to October 15, and 2026 extractions confirm October 15 - November 14 and February foothold windows. The EC number and in-force date of that amendment were not confirmed.

September 2025 Fur Harvesting Regulations amendments: the announced changes (snare prohibition on public land, bait-with-snares prohibition, killing neck snare / live-restraining snare designs, tightened landowner permission, landowner trap-removal right, trapper continuing education by 2029) are recorded from the government news release, but the amended regulation text was not read. Whether the s. 9 trap-check intervals (72 hours / daily / 48 hours), the s. 4 snare specifications, and Schedule C survived the amendments unchanged is unconfirmed. Resolve by reading the current consolidated Fur Harvesting Regulations on princeedwardisland.ca.

Trapping licence fee: Schedule B (last amended EC305/13) sets $10 adult / $5 junior (HST not included). No newer official source stating the trapping licence fee was found - the Trapping Information Centre confirms the WCF fee and course fee but not the licence fee itself. Confirm the current fee at Access PEI or in the 2026 Trapping Summary's licence table.

Junior licence age band is inconsistent across official sources: Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 2(2) says a junior trapping licence is for an applicant 'under 16 years of age', while Schedule B prices a junior licence for '12-17 years of age' and the hunting licence service treats youth as 12-17. Which band governs a junior trapping licence is unconfirmed.

Beaver Restricted Zone (Kensington-Malpeque-Darnley-Fox River-Long River): appears in secondary extractions of the 2026 summary as a named beaver trapping area with the general Nov 1 - Mar 31 dates. What is restricted there (devices, permits, access) was not verified against an official source.

Mandatory trapper harvest reporting: the annual summaries include a Trapper Harvest Log, and fur dealers have statutory monthly reporting duties (s. 13), but whether a licensed trapper must submit a harvest return was not verified in the sources read.
Raccoon night hunting: a secondary extraction of the 2026 summary indicates a permit is required for night hunting of raccoon. Not confirmed in the regulation text read in this pass.

Whether the September 2025 snare rules (public-land prohibition, bait prohibition, design requirements) apply to snowshoe hare snaring under a Snowshoe Hare Snaring Licence was not verified; hare snares are separately specified (single strand brass wire, 20-24 gauge, loop max 10 cm) in the Hunting Summary.
River otter: absence of an open season is certain (not in Schedule II), but whether PEI states an explicit protection instrument for otter beyond that absence was not verified.
Scientific names are standard taxonomy and are not stated in PEI's regulations (scientific_name_verified is false throughout, per convention).

aihts.models_note: Unlike Ontario, PEI's Schedule C model lists are short enough to transcribe in full, and they are transcribed above from the 2015 office consolidation of the Fur Harvesting Regulations. The current Schedule C may have been amended since 2015 (the schedule's amendment trail ends at EC539/15 in the consolidation read); re-verify against the current consolidation before launch. Certification is not the same as current manufacturing: several listed models are legacy/discontinued. Do not present the list as a shopping list without a retailer-availability check (not done in this pass).
aihts.note: PEI implements AIHTS through its own Schedule C of the Fur Harvesting Regulations (EC663/04): 'List of Approved Body-Gripping Traps (Certified under the Canadian Trap Certification Program and Approved for use as Killing Traps for Beaver, Muskrat, Raccoon and Weasel in Prince Edward Island)'. CONFIRMED: PEI adopts the Fur Institute of Canada / Canadian Trap Certification Program certified list, but only as filtered through Schedule C - a trap certified nationally is NOT legal for these species in PEI unless it appears in Schedule C. The requirement covers body-gripping (killing) traps only: on land for beaver, raccoon, muskrat and weasel (s. 5(6)), and underwater for beaver and muskrat (s. 5(7)). PEI has NO certified restraining-trap schedule; restraining traps are governed by design standards instead (modified foot-hold traps for coyote/fox, padded or foot-encapsulating traps for raccoon, drowning sets for beaver/mink/muskrat). Snares are not AIHTS-certified devices; since September 2025 PEI requires killing neck snare designs or live-restraining snares and prohibits snares on public land (announced changes; amended text not read in this pass). AIHTS was agreed in 1997 and ratified by Canada in June 1999; the FIC maintains the national certified-trap list (updated July 22, 2026).
trap_rules: Body-gripping traps used to take beaver, raccoon, muskrat or weasel on land must be approved traps listed in Schedule C (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 5(6)); the same applies underwater for beaver and muskrat, except a muskrat set that prevents resurfacing (s. 5(7)).
Body-gripping traps with jaw spread greater than 16 cm may be set only in or over water, in a dog-proof enclosure meeting the standards in s. 5(3)-(4), or at least 1.5 m off the ground (s. 5(2)).

Foot-hold traps: for beaver, mink or muskrat they must be attached to a drowning device (s. 6(1)(a)-(b)); for raccoon, jaws must be rubber-padded or the trap foot-encapsulating (s. 6(1)(d)); for coyote or red fox, jaws must be laminated, off-set, padded, or similarly modified (s. 6(1)(e) - the 'modified foot-hold trap'). No running pole or spring pole sets with foot-hold traps (s. 6(3)).

Permitted devices in wildlife habitat during open season are limited to: box traps; body-gripping traps designed to kill quickly; submarine traps; non-powered snares; steel-jawed traps with jaw spread under 19 cm; and foot-encapsulating traps (s. 8(2)). Toothed traps, deadfalls and hooks are prohibited (s. 7).

Snares (pre-September-2025 text): wire no larger than single strand brass wire of 20 gauge except during the fox/coyote snaring season (s. 4(1)); heavier snares need a self-locking device (s. 4(2)); no snare for coyote or red fox within 50 m of a bait unless the bait is concealed from the air or in an open field (s. 4(5)); no fox/coyote snare in a highway right-of-way (s. 4(6)); no snare within 200 m of an occupied dwelling without the occupier's permission, or a baited snare within 300 m (s. 9(1)(k)-(l)); fox/coyote snare wire minimum 1.98 mm (s. 9(1)(m)). September 2025 changes prohibit snares on public land and bait used with snares and restrict snares to killing neck snare or live-restraining designs (news release; amended text not read).

Trap-check intervals (s. 9(1)(h)-(i)): every trapping device must be examined at least once every 72 hours; traps designed to hold an animal alive must be examined at least once a day; snares designed to kill red fox or coyote must be examined at least once every 48 hours.

Every trap or snare must be clearly identified with the trapper's permanent trapper registration number (s. 2(4)-(5)). Metal dies are no longer required (2020 Hunting and Trapping Summary) but the ID marking requirement stands.

No trap may be placed in wildlife habitat before the first day of the open season for that species or left after its close (s. 8(1)). In February and March, beaver, muskrat and mink traps may be set only in or over water (s. 9(1)(d)); in March, weasel traps must be Victor rat traps (s. 9(1)(e)).

Trapping is restricted or closed on listed public lands (about 3,525 hectares closed province-wide, including demonstration woodlots, natural areas and trail properties named on the Trapping Information Centre page). Since September 2025, landowners may remove traps set on their property without permission, and permission standards for traps and snares on private land were tightened (news release).

aihts.canada_wide: AIHTS in force in Canada since 1 June 1999 (Canada, the EU and Russia are parties; the US is not a party). FIC-certified traps mandatory per Phase 1 lists - killing traps: beaver, Canada lynx & bobcat, fisher, marten, muskrat (on land and underwater), otter, raccoon, weasels/ermine; restraining traps: beaver (cage), bobcat, Canada lynx, raccoon, wolf. Conventional steel-jawed leghold restraining traps on land are effectively banned for AIHTS species. Killing neck snares are NOT AIHTS traps and are not FIC-certified; provinces regulate snares separately. [R1 s.2a]
aihts.jurisdiction_specific: Prince Edward Island is a FIC Note 1 province (exclusive use of certified restraining traps for raccoon). [R1 s.2a]

check_interval.live_holding: Live-holding traps: daily. All trapping devices: at least once every 72 hours (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 9(1)(h)-(i)).
check_interval.killing: Every 72 hours generally; snares designed to kill red fox/coyote: every 48 hours.
check_interval.note: Verified in regulation text (R2 Item 2); supersedes R1's unverified secondary summary of 'every 2-3 days'.

canada_only.tenure: No tenure system - small, private-land-dominated province; landowner permission required before setting any traps.
canada_only.trap_id_requirement: REQUIRED - every trap and snare must be clearly identified with the trapper's permanent trapper registration number (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 2(4)-(5)); possessing unmarked snares in wildlife habitat is also barred (s. 4(4)). Verified in regulation text. [R2 Item 6]
canada_only.nuisance_route: Department-issued nuisance permits to designated trappers (a nuisance beaver permit removing roughly 140-200 beavers a year; a nuisance coyote permit, 5 or fewer a year since 2020). Relocating problem beavers is not accepted - removal is lethal. No standing paid-operator licence; whether permit trappers are paid is not stated in the sources. [R2 Item 3]
canada_only.harvest_reporting_and_sealing: NONE - no mandatory trapper harvest report and no pelt sealing requirement in the Fur Harvesting Regulations (verified in regulation text). Instead: possession of a green hide/carcass from 5 days after season close to the next open season is prohibited without a Minister's permit (s. 10); fur dealers (not trappers) must report purchases monthly (s. 13); harvest data comes from a voluntary phone survey. [R2 Item 2]
